note: Cascade Valley University catalogue: 1 university, 10 programs, 50 courses with syllabus topics

programs.name: Nursing
programs.description: Pre-licensure nursing degree combining science foundations, clinical reasoning and supervised practice across adult, maternal and community settings.

programs.name: Public Health
programs.description: Undergraduate degree focused on population health, epidemiology, health policy and community-based prevention.

programs.name: History
programs.school: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
programs.description: Study of the human past through primary sources, historiography and argumentative writing across regions and periods.

programs.name: English Literature
programs.school: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
programs.description: Close reading, critical theory and writing across British, American and world literatures.

programs.name: Political Science
programs.school: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
programs.description: Study of governments, political behaviour, international relations and public policy using comparative and empirical methods.

programs.name: Sociology
programs.school: College of Humanities and Social Sciences
programs.description: Study of social structure, inequality, institutions and social change using qualitative and quantitative research.

programs.name: Chemistry
programs.description: Laboratory-intensive degree covering general, organic, analytical and physical chemistry.

programs.name: Physics
programs.description: Foundational physics from mechanics to quantum theory with strong mathematical and laboratory training.

programs.name: Civil Engineering
programs.description: Engineering of infrastructure including structures, geotechnical systems, water resources and transportation.

programs.name: Graphic Design
programs.description: Studio-based degree in visual communication, typography, branding and digital design.

courses.name: Foundations of Nursing Practice
courses.description: Introduces the professional role of the nurse, the nursing process and basic patient care skills. Includes a supervised skills laboratory.
courses.learningOutcomes: Describe the nursing process; demonstrate basic assessment and hygiene skills; explain professional and ethical standards of practice.

topics.title: The nursing process
topics.description: Assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation and evaluation as a framework for patient care.

topics.title: Vital signs and basic assessment
topics.description: Measuring and interpreting temperature, pulse, respiration, blood pressure and pain in the skills laboratory.

topics.title: Professional standards and ethics
topics.description: Scope of practice, patient rights, confidentiality, informed consent and the code of ethics for nurses.

topics.title: Infection prevention and safety
topics.description: Hand hygiene, standard precautions, patient positioning and fall prevention.

courses.name: Health Assessment
courses.description: Develops systematic history-taking and physical examination skills across body systems and the lifespan.
courses.learningOutcomes: Obtain a comprehensive health history; perform a head-to-toe examination; document findings accurately.

topics.title: Health history interviewing
topics.description: Structured interviewing, cultural sensitivity and communication techniques for collecting subjective data.

topics.title: Physical examination by body system
topics.description: Inspection, palpation, percussion and auscultation of the cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal and neurological systems.

topics.title: Assessment across the lifespan
topics.description: Adapting assessment for infants, children, adults and older adults.

topics.title: Clinical documentation
topics.description: Recording objective findings and recognizing abnormal results that require escalation.

courses.name: Pharmacology for Nursing
courses.description: Covers drug classifications, mechanisms of action, safe administration and patient teaching.
courses.learningOutcomes: Calculate dosages accurately; explain major drug classes and adverse effects; apply the rights of medication administration.

topics.title: Principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics
topics.description: Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion and how they shape dosing.

topics.title: Dosage calculation and safe administration
topics.description: Dimensional analysis, oral and parenteral routes, and the rights of medication administration.

topics.title: Major drug classes
topics.description: Cardiovascular, antimicrobial, analgesic, endocrine and psychotropic agents and their nursing implications.

topics.title: Patient teaching and adverse reactions
topics.description: Monitoring for side effects, interactions and educating patients about adherence.

courses.name: Adult Health Nursing I
courses.description: Care of adults with acute and chronic medical-surgical conditions, with clinical placement hours.
courses.learningOutcomes: Plan care for adults with common medical-surgical conditions; prioritize interventions; evaluate outcomes in clinical settings.

topics.title: Pathophysiology of common adult conditions
topics.description: Cardiac, respiratory, renal and endocrine disorders and their clinical manifestations.

topics.title: Perioperative nursing care
topics.description: Preoperative teaching, intraoperative safety and postoperative monitoring and recovery.

topics.title: Clinical reasoning and prioritization
topics.description: Using data to set priorities and respond to patient deterioration.

courses.name: Maternal and Child Nursing
courses.description: Nursing care of childbearing families and children from infancy through adolescence.
courses.learningOutcomes: Describe normal pregnancy, labor and newborn care; assess child growth and development; plan family-centered care.

topics.title: Antepartum, intrapartum and postpartum care
topics.description: Physiological changes of pregnancy, stages of labor and recovery after birth.

topics.title: Newborn assessment and care
topics.description: Apgar scoring, thermoregulation, feeding and screening of the healthy newborn.

topics.title: Growth and development in childhood
topics.description: Developmental milestones and age-appropriate communication with children and families.

courses.name: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: Surveys the history, core functions and ethical foundations of public health and the determinants of population health.
courses.learningOutcomes: Define the core functions of public health; identify social determinants of health; discuss historical public health achievements.

topics.title: History and core functions of public health
topics.description: Sanitation, vaccination and tobacco control as milestones, and the assessment, policy and assurance functions.

topics.title: Determinants of health
topics.description: Social, economic, environmental and behavioural influences on health outcomes.

topics.title: Health disparities and equity
topics.description: Measuring and explaining differences in health between population groups.

topics.title: Public health systems and ethics
topics.description: Roles of local, national and global agencies and ethical frameworks for population interventions.

courses.name: Epidemiology
courses.description: Introduces the study of the distribution and determinants of disease in populations, including study design and measures of association.
courses.learningOutcomes: Calculate incidence and prevalence; compare study designs; interpret risk ratios and odds ratios.

topics.title: Measures of disease frequency
topics.description: Incidence, prevalence, rates and age standardization.

topics.title: Study designs
topics.description: Cohort, case-control, cross-sectional and randomized trials, with strengths and limitations of each.

topics.title: Bias, confounding and causation
topics.description: Sources of systematic error and criteria for causal inference.

topics.title: Outbreak investigation
topics.description: Steps for investigating an outbreak and constructing an epidemic curve.

courses.name: Biostatistics for Health Sciences
courses.description: Applied statistics for health data, emphasizing descriptive methods, inference and regression.
courses.learningOutcomes: Summarize health data; conduct hypothesis tests and confidence intervals; fit and interpret simple regression models.

topics.title: Descriptive statistics and data visualization
topics.description: Summarizing continuous and categorical health data with tables and graphs.

topics.title: Probability and sampling distributions
topics.description: Probability rules, normal distribution and the central limit theorem.

topics.title: Confidence intervals and hypothesis testing
topics.description: t-tests, chi-square tests and interpreting p-values in health research.

topics.title: Linear and logistic regression
topics.description: Modeling continuous and binary health outcomes with covariates.

courses.name: Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Examines how health care is financed, organized and regulated, and how policy is made and evaluated.
courses.learningOutcomes: Describe health system structures; analyze a health policy proposal; explain basic health financing mechanisms.

topics.title: Health system organization and financing
topics.description: Insurance models, payment mechanisms and the roles of public and private payers.

topics.title: The policy-making process
topics.description: Agenda setting, legislation, implementation and evaluation of health policy.

topics.title: Access, quality and cost
topics.description: Frameworks for measuring access to care, quality of care and cost containment.

courses.name: Community Health Education
courses.description: Theory and practice of designing, delivering and evaluating health education programs for communities.
courses.learningOutcomes: Apply behaviour-change theories; design a program logic model; evaluate a community intervention.

topics.title: Health behaviour theories
topics.description: The health belief model, social cognitive theory and stages of change.

topics.title: Needs assessment and program planning
topics.description: Collecting community data to set priorities and write program objectives.

topics.title: Program evaluation
topics.description: Process and outcome evaluation, indicators and reporting to stakeholders.

courses.name: World History to 1500
courses.description: Surveys the major civilizations, trade networks and belief systems of the world from early agriculture to 1500.
courses.learningOutcomes: Compare early civilizations; explain patterns of cultural exchange; analyze a primary source in context.

topics.title: Classical empires and belief systems

topics.title: Trade networks and cultural exchange
topics.description: The Silk Roads, Indian Ocean trade and Trans-Saharan commerce.

topics.title: Medieval societies
topics.description: Feudal Europe, the Islamic caliphates, Byzantium and the Mongol empire.

courses.name: World History since 1500
courses.description: Covers global transformations from the early modern era to the present, including empire, industrialization and decolonization.
courses.learningOutcomes: Trace major global transformations; evaluate causes of revolutions; interpret competing historical narratives.

topics.title: Early modern empires and exchange

topics.title: Revolutions and nation-states

topics.title: Imperialism and world wars

topics.title: Decolonization and globalization

courses.description: Examines the colonial era, the American Revolution, the early republic, slavery and the Civil War and Reconstruction.

topics.title: Colonial societies and the Revolution
topics.description: Settlement patterns, imperial conflict and the revolutionary movement.

topics.title: The early republic

topics.title: Slavery, sectionalism and Civil War
topics.description: Slave economy, abolition, secession and the war.

topics.title: Reconstruction
topics.description: Emancipation, constitutional amendments and the contest over citizenship.

courses.name: Historiography and Research Methods
courses.description: Introduces approaches to historical interpretation and trains students in archival research and scholarly writing.
courses.learningOutcomes: Compare historiographical schools; locate and evaluate primary sources; write a documented research paper.

topics.title: Schools of historical interpretation

topics.title: Finding and evaluating sources
topics.description: Archives, databases and source criticism.

topics.title: Citation and scholarly argument

topics.title: Industrial society and ideologies

topics.title: Total war and the postwar order

courses.name: College Writing and Rhetoric

topics.title: Rhetorical situations

topics.title: Source use and academic integrity

topics.title: Marxist, feminist and psychoanalytic criticism

topics.title: Postcolonial and cultural theory

topics.title: Parties, elections and public opinion

topics.title: War, security and deterrence

topics.title: International political economy

topics.title: The policy cycle
topics.description: Problem definition, agenda setting, adoption and implementation.

topics.title: Policy instruments and cost-benefit analysis

topics.title: Policy writing

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology

topics.title: Social stratification

topics.title: Survey research and sampling

topics.title: Qualitative methods

topics.title: Symbolic interactionism and everyday life

topics.title: Social determinants of illness

topics.title: The experience of illness

topics.title: Medicine as an institution
